risks.note: Ranked the top material issue. Any lapse in food safety protocols could lead to legal liabilities, damage to brand reputation and loss of customer trust; proper handling and hygiene are critical to prevent contamination and foodborne illness. Mitigation: food safety protocols embedded across menu development, packaging, distribution and restaurant operations; monthly sensory evaluation of key products and quarterly for non-key products; technology and automation aligned to food-safety standards. Stated financial implication: negative.

Westlife sources ingredients from many suppliers, so food safety depends on supply-chain management, and the business affects environmental health, animal welfare and livelihoods. Disruptions or inconsistencies in supplier practices directly hit menu quality and availability. Stated financial implication: negative — timely availability of products can be compromised by value-chain disruption, and operational inconsistency damages reputation and profitability. Mitigation: sustainable/ethical sourcing, supplier selection on quality, sustainable farming and labour rights, and Supply Chain Human Rights Audits (SCHRA) for every supplier covering business integrity, child labour and forced labour.
risks.risk: Responsible sourcing and supplier practices (supply-chain concentration and disruption)

risks.note: Evolving consumer awareness demands accessible nutritional information and clear labelling; failure damages brand reputation and attracts regulatory scrutiny, impacting sales and profitability. Mitigation: artificial colours, preservatives and flavourings eliminated from select/most items; allergen and nutritional information displayed in-store and on the McDelivery app; fat and sodium reduced in key products; strict advertising guidelines; nutrition-focused innovation including the Multi-Millets Bun and Protein Plus Slice.
risks.risk: Nutrition and responsible marketing / regulatory scrutiny of food labelling

risks.note: A large volume of customer data is captured for operational purposes through the McDonald's app, McDelivery and self-ordering kiosks — a risk that scales with the Company's own digital strategy, given digital channels contribute 76% of sales. A breach can lead to fines, penalties and reputational damage. Mitigation: Cybersecurity and Privacy Policy on the intranet, robust security measures, and cyber security explicitly within the Risk Management Committee's monitoring mandate.

The Company itself states the business is 'relatively energy-intensive due to usage of commercial kitchen appliances and high volumes', with temperature-controlled dining areas. Stated financial implication: negative — physical assets such as facilities and logistics infrastructure are at risk of damage from extreme weather events with substantial repair and replacement cost, and regulatory change could raise operating and compliance costs. Mitigation: energy-efficiency upgrades, process optimisation to reduce carbon footprint, and renewable energy including solar. Note the tension with the standalone Directors' Report line that 'the operations of your Company are not energy intensive' and that capital investment on energy-conservation equipment was NIL — that statement is made for the listed holding entity, with the measures attributed to the subsidiary HRPL.

Human-rights violations can cause operational delays, lawsuits, poor employee satisfaction and reputational damage. Mitigation: policies, training and regular audits; zero-tolerance approach to compulsory and forced labour including human trafficking and child labour; human-rights clauses in all business agreements and contracts.
risks.risk: Human rights across own operations and the value chain

risks.note: Compliance with evolving food and nutrition regulations, legal norms and ethical standards has a direct impact on business operations and brand image. Mitigation: Standards of Business Conduct, Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption Policy, Code of Conduct and whistleblower mechanisms, an internal committee reviewing food-nutrition compliance, and 100% of operations assessed for corruption-related risks within the ERM framework. Nil disciplinary actions for bribery/corruption against directors, KMPs or employees, and nil conflict-of-interest complaints, in FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25.
risks.risk: Ethics and compliance in an evolving food-regulation regime

risks.note: Water conservation is stated as necessary for regulatory compliance, lower operating cost and business continuity, with water shortages capable of interrupting operations and breaching regulatory norms; waste from daily operations is called a significant environmental challenge in the industry, exposing the Company to fines, higher disposal costs and increased expenses. Mitigation: waterless urinals, reuse of RO-rejected water, high-water-recovery RO systems in all restaurants, spray faucets (stated to reduce water consumption by 50-80%), packaging optimisation, safe disposal and operations training.
risks.risk: Water and waste management (resource and regulatory exposure at restaurant level)
